children: Chevron will divest its ownership interests in Hess Midstream and DJ Basin midstream assets and expects a one-time after-tax loss of $3 to $4 billion while cutting Bakken midstream costs by ~50%.
Chevron will transfer its Hess Midstream ownership and GP position plus DJ Basin assets in exchange for improved Bakken terms and $200M cash.
Revised Bakken contracts are expected to reduce Chevron’s Bakken unit midstream costs by ~50%, improving earnings and ROCE.
Chevron expects to deconsolidate Hess Midstream at closing, including ~ $3.7B of Hess Midstream debt.
At closing Chevron expects a one-time after-tax loss of approximately $3–$4B, to be treated as a special item.
Transaction subject to customary conditions and regulatory approvals and is expected to close by year-end 2026.
